claims.text: The initial alloy is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
A crack-free, continuous Al2O3 coating can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by a process such as PVD.
The deposited alumina coating will be thin and adherent.
The alumina layer will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier at the alloy surface.
The alumina coating will prevent or significantly slow oxygen ingress into the bulk alloy.
Slower oxygen ingress will limit internal oxidation that degrades high-temperature performance.
The coating will leave the intrinsic mechanical properties of the alloy microstructure unaffected.
After 50 hours at 1000 °C in air, coated samples will have lower oxygen uptake and less oxide-scale formation than uncoated samples.
After oxidation exposure, coated samples will retain room-temperature ductility similar to untreated cast alloy.
After oxidation exposure, coated samples will retain high-temperature yield strength similar to untreated cast alloy at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Uncoated samples exposed at high temperature in air will undergo significant oxidation that ultimately compromises mechanical integrity.
Coating thickness, adhesion quality, and degradation under cyclic thermal loading may affect protection.
